description_en: Bhirat Darbāra Temple 1 is part of a complex that also includes two stone monuments surrounded by a stone wall. The site is located on top of a mountain directly to the west of the Gotijyula village, at an elevation of 2390 meters (7841 ft.). The summit of the massif is crowned by a vast open grassy area used for religious festivals and picnics. The entire area is thought to be the site of the Durbar of a king named Bhirat, or Birat. The historical identity of this character could not be determined at this time. Nonetheless, it is important to note that no architectural remnants have been discovered on the area's surface. The two structures are located at the northern end of the summit. A steep cliff lies directly north of them.Temple 1 is a recently reconstructed square room with a central door on each side. These doors face north-east, south-east, south-west, and north-west. The room has a corbelled roof with a central opening. A tree trunk is inserted through the opening. The corbelled dome is supported at each corner by spandrels resting on roughly cut stone pillars. The base of the tree rests at the centre of the sanctum. The entire stone structure is made of dry masonry. Roughly cut stones are laid on the floor to make a pavement.South of this monument is a half-buried square structure (JUM0481), also built with local stones and dry masonry. The exact purpose and origin of these two structures, known locally as temples, are unknown at this time. None of the existing material found in situ appears to have been carved more than approximately 100-200 years ago. During the month of Śravaṇa (July-August), annual worship is held here.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired), Rebuilt
